title: Tenant isolation escrow and in-path fallback proxy hotfix
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: reduce tenant oscillation during short bursts by introducing an escrowed isolation token and an in-path fallback proxy that temporarily brokers requests while a tenant quarantine settles. Improves regional failover stability and SLO preservation.
body: Context: during a multi-region incident we observed repeated short-lived tenant quarantines that caused oscillating routing decisions and amplified downstream load on fallback regions. This PR introduces an escrowed tenant isolation token plus a lightweight fallback proxy to reduce churn and provide a deterministic short-term routing behavior. Motivation: prevent rapid circuit flips and cross-region amplification for tenants that spike transiently, preserve P95/P99 latency SLOs for healthy tenants, and give operators a safe, fast rollback path. Design summary: 1) Escrow token: when the SLO enforcer decides to quarantine a tenant, it issues a time-limited escrow token representing the quarantine window. The token is stored in the regional state with an expiry and a small grace buffer to avoid immediate reopens. 2) In-path fallback proxy: requests for escrowed tenants are routed through a tiny proxy layer that implements controlled rate shaping, request buffering for short windows (<3s), and a deterministic fallback decision based on token age and current region health metrics. 3) Backoff smoothing: quarantine reopen uses exponential backoff with jitter and a minimum stabilization window to avoid flip-flopping. 4) Observability: new rollup metrics (quarantine_issued, escrow_active, fallback_proxy_routed, proxy_drop_rate) and traces (escrow.issue, fallbackproxy.route) are emitted. Implementation notes: changes touch the SLO enforcer state machine (slo/enforcer.go), regional routing mesh (routing/fallback_proxy.go), telemetry (telemetry/rollups.go), and the smoke test harness (test/e2e/quarantine_simulation_test.go). The fallback proxy is intentionally lightweight (single-file implementation) and uses existing request-shim infrastructure; it performs a constant-time token lookup and a bounded queue before forwarding. Compatibility: existing rollout policies and canary flags are respected via config flag slo.escrow_enabled defaulting to false for controlled rollout. Tests and validation: added unit tests for token lifecycle (slo/enforcer_test.go) and property tests for the proxy queue under bursty arrival patterns. End-to-end simulation harness reproduces the incident pattern and demonstrates reduced cross-region failover events in 10/10 trial runs. CI: lint, unit, integration, and canary-sim checks passed locally and in CI. Risk and rollback: low risk due to flag gating; rollback is a config flip (slo.escrow_enabled=false) and immediate draining of any active escrow tokens. We included a safety circuit that rejects the proxy path if proxy_drop_rate exceeds 5% for more than 30s to prevent user-facing errors. Ops and deployment notes: staged rollout to us-west-2 and eu-central-1 only, follow with metrics alert slo.escrow_active > 100 in a region and sustained proxy_drop_rate > 2% to halt rollout. Linear/Jira: ENG-4321 describes the long-term mitigation; SUP-1187 is the customer-facing support ticket that prompted the hotfix. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked and reviewed - [x] Unit tests added - [x] E2E simulation added - [x] Metrics and traces emitted - [x] Feature flag gating implemented - [x] Rollout plan and rollback tested

Review conversation summary: Miguel: Asked for clarification on token expiry semantics and whether expiry is absolute or sliding; author clarified it's absolute with a small 250ms grace to absorb coordination lag.
Lena: Requested an additional circuit to protect the proxy when upstream latency increases; added proxy_drop_rate circuit and a short-circuit path back to normal routing.
Omar: Noted potential metric cardinality cost; we restricted trace labels to tenant buckets and emitted rollups to avoid high cardinality.
